key_decisions.rationale: Keeps Paul's self-reference and quotes the opponents' characterization.
key_decisions.before: Now I, Paul, myself appeal to you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ—I who am humble when face to face with you, but bold toward you when absent—
key_decisions.after: Now I, Paul, personally appeal to you by Christ's gentleness and graciousness—I who am “humble” when face-to-face with you, but “bold” toward you when absent.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Now I, Paul, myself appeal to you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ—I who am humble when face to face with you, but bold toward you when absent—

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves requested avoidance, anticipated action, and accusation.
key_decisions.before: I beg that when I am present I may not have to be bold with the confidence by which I consider showing boldness against some who think of us as walking according to the flesh.
key_decisions.after: I ask that, when present, I will not have to be bold with the confidence I expect to show against some who think we walk according to the flesh.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: I beg that when I am present I may not have to be bold with the confidence by which I consider showing boldness against some who think of us as walking according to the flesh.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps embodied life distinct from fleshly warfare.
key_decisions.before: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh,
key_decisions.after: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh,

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves military metaphor and enjambment into the next verse.
key_decisions.before: for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh but have divine power for the tearing down of strongholds.
key_decisions.after: For the weapons of our warfare are not fleshly but powerful through God for tearing down strongholds. We tear down arguments
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh but have divine power for the tearing down of strongholds.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps elevated resistance, captivity, and directed obedience.
key_decisions.before: We tear down arguments and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and we take every thought captive to the obedience of Christ,
key_decisions.after: and every proud obstacle raised against the knowledge of God, and we take every thought captive to obey Christ.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: We tear down arguments and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and we take every thought captive to the obedience of Christ,

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves readiness, punishment, and timing condition.
key_decisions.before: being ready to punish every disobedience, when your obedience is complete.
key_decisions.after: And we are ready to punish every disobedience once your obedience is complete.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: being ready to punish every disobedience, when your obedience is complete.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps possible command, self-examination, and equal claim.
key_decisions.before: Look at what is before your eyes. If someone is confident that he belongs to Christ, let him consider again that just as he belongs to Christ, so also do we.
key_decisions.after: Look at what is right in front of you. If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ, he should consider this again about himself: just as he belongs to Christ, so do we.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Look at what is before your eyes. If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ, let him consider again that just as he belongs to Christ, so also do we.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves authority's source and constructive limit.
key_decisions.before: For even if I boast somewhat excessively about our authority, which the Lord gave for building you up and not for tearing you down, I will not be put to shame.
key_decisions.after: For even if I boast somewhat more about our authority, which the Lord gave for building you up and not tearing you down, I will not be ashamed.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For even if I boast somewhat excessively about our authority, which the Lord gave for building you up and not for tearing you down, I will not be put to shame.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the opponent's disparaging words and bodily reference.
key_decisions.before: For they say, “His letters are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech of no account.”
key_decisions.after: For someone says, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his bodily presence is weak and his speech amounts to nothing.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For they say, “His letters are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech of no account.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps Paul's irony and repeated self-comparison.
key_decisions.before: For we do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves; but when they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they are without understanding.
key_decisions.after: For we do not dare to place or compare ourselves with some who recommend themselves. But when they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they lack understanding.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For we do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves; but when they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they are without understanding.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves measured field and divine assignment.
key_decisions.before: But we will not boast beyond measure, but within the measure of the sphere that God has assigned to us—a measure that reaches even to you.
key_decisions.after: We, however, will not boast beyond measure, but only according to the boundary God assigned to us—a boundary that extends even as far as you.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But we will not boast beyond measure, but within the measure of the sphere that God has assigned to us—a measure that reaches even to you.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves denial, growth, and bounded expansion.
key_decisions.before: We do not boast beyond measure in the labors of others, but our hope is that as your trust increases, our sphere among you may be enlarged still more,
key_decisions.after: We do not boast beyond measure in the labors of others. But we hope that as your faith grows, our work among you will be greatly enlarged within our boundary,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: We do not boast beyond measure in the labors of others, but our hope is that as your faith increases, our sphere among you may be enlarged still more,

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps future mission and refusal to claim another's labor.
key_decisions.before: so that we may proclaim the good news in lands beyond you, without boasting in work already done in another’s sphere.
key_decisions.after: so that we may proclaim the gospel in the regions beyond you, without boasting about work already prepared in someone else's field.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: so that we may proclaim the good news in lands beyond you, without boasting in work already done in another’s sphere.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps self-commendation and divine approval contrast.
key_decisions.before: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
key_decisions.after: For it is not the one who recommends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord recommends.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
